content.title: Spurs vs. Grizzlies: Prediction, How to Watch for Free (3/25/26)
content.text: The San Antonio Spurs (54–18) face the Memphis Grizzlies (24–47) tonight at FedExForum in Memphis. The Spurs are surging, having won six straight. But the Oklahoma City Thunder have also stayed red-hot, extending their own winning streak to 12 games. As a result, the Spurs remain three games behind OKC in what has long been a two-team race for the top seed in the Western Conference. San Antonio trimmed the gap just a bit while Shai Gilgeous-Alexander was sidelined, but the margin has largely held steady. Still, the Spurs are closing in on locking up the No. 2 seed, and a matchup with the struggling Grizzlies presents a prime opportunity to strengthen that position. San Antonio enters tonight’s contest following an emphatic 136–111 victory over the Miami Heat on Monday. Victor Wembanyama led the way with 26 points, 15 rebounds, and five blocks, while Keldon Johnson and rookie Dylan Harper added 21 points apiece. Stephon Castle chipped in 19 as part of a balanced offensive performance. The Spurs were particularly dominant on the glass, outrebounding Miami 62–38 and grabbing 17 offensive rebounds. Memphis, meanwhile, has dropped three straight since its surprising 125–118 win over the Denver Nuggets last Wednesday. The Grizzlies were routed 146–107 by the Atlanta Hawks on Monday, as Atlanta placed eight players in double figures and knocked down 25 three-pointers. GG Jackson paced Memphis with 26 points on 9-of-14 shooting, while Tyler Burton added 20. Rookie Walter Clayton Jr. contributed 16 points and six assists but struggled with efficiency, shooting just 4-of-13 from the field. Expect a comfortable double-digit win for the Spurs, who could approach — or surpass — the 130-point mark against a Memphis defense that has struggled badly in recent weeks. Final Score Prediction: San Antonio Spurs 130, Memphis Grizzlies 108 Injury Report San Antonio Spurs Luke Kornet — Out (Knee) De’Aaron Fox — Out (Back) David Jones Garcia — Out (Ankle) Memphis Grizzlies Zach Edey — Out (Ankle) Ja Morant — Out (Elbow) Brandon Clarke — Out (Calf) Javon Small — GTD (Back) Jahmai Mashack — Out (Ankle) Jaylen Wells — Out (Toe) Ty Jerome — Out (Ankle) Santi Aldama — Out (Knee) Scotty Pippen Jr. — Out (Toe) Kentavious Caldwell-Pope — Out (Finger) How to Watch Spurs vs. Grizzlies Tip-off for tonight’s Spurs-Grizzlies game is set for 8:00 PM Eastern / 7:00 PM Central at the FedExForum in Memphis.
